# webtables/str

> String literal: a passive data segment, copied to the heap on first use.

truck [webtables](../webtables.md) · [source](../../../registry/webtables/str.pkg)

WebAssembly text has no way to name the address of data, so each literal
is a passive segment (`{hex}` is its bytes as `\hh` escapes) and a global
holding its address, 0 until the first use. Then `$__pk_str` allocates
the length, the bytes and a 0, the layout every backend uses, and
`memory.init` copies the bytes in.

## Emit variants

The first variant whose condition holds is used.

### `emit`

```nasm
(block (result i64)
(if (i64.eqz (global.get ${D.p})) (then
(global.set ${D.p} (call $__pk_str (i64.const {len})))
(memory.init ${D.s} (i32.add (i32.wrap_i64 (global.get ${D.p})) (i32.const 8)) (i32.const 0) (i32.const {len}))))
(global.get ${D.p}))
@alloc
```

Includes: [webtables/alloc](alloc.md)

## Data (per use)

```nasm
(data ${D.s} "{hex}")
(global ${D.p} (mut i64) (i64.const 0))
```
